# `silk/crypto/p521`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Key agreement (ECDH) and ECDSA signatures on the NIST P-521 curve (secp521r1).

## When to use
Use [`P521`](#P521) for an ECDH key exchange where a protocol needs P-521, such as a TLS key share
`secp521r1`, and to sign with ECDSA, as in `ES512` JSON Web Tokens or Node.js `crypto.sign`. Use
[`EcdsaP521Sha512`](#EcdsaP521Sha512) to verify a DER signature with SHA-512, for example in a certificate chain,
and [`EcdsaP521`](#EcdsaP521) to verify with another hash or in the fixed 132-byte form.

## Details
Public keys are 133 bytes in uncompressed SEC1 form: `0x04`, then the X and Y coordinates, each
66 bytes big-endian. [`P521.compressPublicKey`](#P521.impl.compressPublicKey) and [`P521.decompressPublicKey`](#P521.impl.decompressPublicKey) convert to and
from the 67-byte compressed form. Secrets are 66 bytes big-endian. [`P521.agree`](#P521.impl.agree) returns the X
coordinate of the shared point and consumes the key. [`P521.sign`](#P521.impl.sign) returns `r` and `s`, each 66
bytes, with the deterministic nonce of RFC 6979. [`EcdsaP521.toDer`](#EcdsaP521.impl.toDer) and [`EcdsaP521.fromDer`](#EcdsaP521.impl.fromDer)
convert signatures to and from DER, which uses the long length form once it reaches 128 bytes.
Nothing allocates.

## Errors
- [`P521Error`](#P521Error) for a secret or a peer public key that is not valid.
- [`P521SignatureError`](#P521SignatureError) for a key or signature that is not valid, or that does not match.

## Gotchas
A valid signature proves only that the holder of the private key signed the message. It does not
prove that you can trust the key. To check a certificate chain, use the `silk.tls.trust_*`
modules. The key exchange does not authenticate the peer. Pass the shared secret through
`silk.crypto.hkdf` before you use it as a key. The secret is not erased when it is dropped.

## Examples
### Verify a signature
```silk
import silk.crypto.p521 { EcdsaP521Sha512, P521SignatureError }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // A public key and a signature of "hello" that another program made.
  let publicKey = b"\x04\x01\x09\x35\x81\x03\x35\x7f\xdc\xf8\x0c\x5e\x61\x84\x4d\x16\x04\x0d\xc8\x11\x6d\x07\x6c\x5d\xe7\x6e\xbf\xb8\x62\x0b\xfb\xb7\xed\xe4\x4f\xac\x0e\x14\x3b\x38\x84\x86\xd5\xee\xba\x44\x08\x04\xb9\xb5\x2b\xfb\xa8\x0d\xb5\x6f\x6d\x05\xab\xf0\xa6\xab\x57\x5f\x64\xb5\x0a\x00\x9b\x1f\x6d\x81\xb3\x9a\xed\x92\xda\xf5\x57\xd6\xb0\xee\x52\x97\x08\x68\x9e\x57\x96\xd2\xce\x4f\xbf\x27\xdd\xd4\x84\x4b\x7c\x36\xc4\xc7\x4c\x70\x93\x75\x66\x6b\x19\x86\x30\xb2\xc4\xce\x07\x09\xd7\x49\x7f\xcc\x84\x2d\xe9\xf2\x7f\xd1\xd7\xb5\x1e\x42\x1f\xb4\xbc"
  let signature = b"\x30\x81\x88\x02\x42\x01\xc3\x1d\x1f\x68\x33\x73\xf0\x26\x23\xd2\xf5\x43\xc7\x26\x69\xa8\x52\x5a\x28\x27\x44\x48\xdd\xfb\x54\x55\x33\xc3\xc8\x9f\x15\x0b\xea\x81\x53\xac\xc6\xa6\xd8\xcc\xa5\xaf\xcf\x7a\x59\x79\xc1\x2f\x9c\xe3\x4b\xe9\xeb\xae\x41\x4c\x18\xe8\xdb\x20\xf1\x1e\x09\xc9\x24\x02\x42\x00\xe3\xe5\xcf\x10\x5b\x99\xc0\xd6\xc7\x69\x43\x50\x07\xd5\x21\xb5\xa5\x69\xe8\x21\x49\xb4\xc1\x8f\xcc\x40\xfb\x4c\x96\x63\x31\x62\xd7\xc8\x88\xd4\x1a\x94\xd8\x08\xe5\x2e\xf1\xb0\x09\x85\xfe\x40\x8f\x66\xce\x08\xa1\x47\x17\x48\x1e\x60\x03\xd6\xf6\x50\x07\x5f\x84"
  match EcdsaP521Sha512.verify(publicKey, b"hello", signature) {
    Result<(), P521SignatureError>.Success {..} => {}
    Result<(), P521SignatureError>.Failure {..} => {
      return 1
    }
  }

  // The same signature does not match another message.
  return match EcdsaP521Sha512.verify(publicKey, b"hellp", signature) {
    Result<(), P521SignatureError>.Failure { error: P521SignatureError.AuthenticationFailed } => 0
    _ => 1
  }
}
```

### Sign and verify
```silk
import silk.crypto.p521 { EcdsaP521, P521, P521Error, P521SignatureError }
import silk.crypto.sha2 { Sha512 }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // Real programs use `P521.generate()` with a secure `Random` provider.
  let mut secret: [u8; 66] = [0; 66]
  secret[65] = 7
  let key = match P521.fromBytes(&secret) {
    Result<P521, P521Error>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<P521, P521Error>.Failure {..} => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let publicKey = key.publicKey()
  let signature = key.sign<Sha512>(b"hello")
  match EcdsaP521.verify<Sha512>(&publicKey, b"hello", &signature) {
    Result<(), P521SignatureError>.Success {..} => {}
    Result<(), P521SignatureError>.Failure {..} => {
      return 1
    }
  }

  // The DER form, as in X.509 and TLS, has at most 139 bytes.
  let mut der: [u8; 139] = [0; 139]
  let length = EcdsaP521.toDer(&signature, &mut der)
  if der[0] != 0x30 || length > 139 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="P521"></a>

## `P521`

```silk
pub struct P521
```

A P-521 secret, for key agreement and for ECDSA signatures. It is not `Copy`.

### When to use
Use it for an ECDH key exchange where a protocol needs P-521, such as a TLS 1.3 key share
`secp521r1`, or to sign with ECDSA.

### Details
[`P521.agree`](#P521.impl.agree) consumes it, so make a new one for each exchange. [`P521.sign`](#P521.impl.sign) does not. Public keys are 133 bytes in
uncompressed SEC1 form: `0x04`, then the X and Y coordinates, each 66 bytes big-endian. Secrets
are 66 bytes big-endian. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas
The key exchange does not authenticate the peer. Pass the shared secret through
`silk.crypto.hkdf` before you use it as a key. The secret is not erased when it is dropped.

Returns a new random secret, with bytes from the ambient `Random`.

It draws 66 bytes again until the value is valid, so the result is uniform. The `Random`
provider must be cryptographically secure. If it fails, the program stops.

### Method `agree`

```silk
pub fn agree(self: Self, peer: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 66], P521Error>
```

Returns the 66-byte shared secret for the public key `peer`, and consumes the secret.

The result is the big-endian X coordinate of the shared point.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength`, `InvalidEncoding`, or `InvalidPoint` if `peer` is not a valid uncompressed
  public key. The secret is consumed also when it fails.

#### Gotchas
Pass the result through `silk.crypto.hkdf` before you use it as a key.

<a id="P521.impl.sign"></a>

### Method `sign`

```silk
pub fn sign<H: Digest>(self: &Self, message: &[u8]) -> [u8; 132]
```

Returns the ECDSA signature of `message`, hashed with `H`, as 132 bytes: `r`, then `s`, each
66 bytes big-endian.

The nonce is deterministic (RFC 6979) with HMAC over `H`, so the same key, hash, and message
always give the same signature. [`EcdsaP521.toDer`](#EcdsaP521.impl.toDer) converts the result to DER.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if `message` is longer than `H` allows.

<a id="P521.impl.signDigest"></a>

### Method `signDigest`

```silk
pub fn signDigest<H: Digest>(self: &Self, digest: &[u8]) -> [u8; 132]
```

Returns the ECDSA signature of a message whose digest is `digest`, as 132 bytes: `r`, then
`s`, each 66 bytes big-endian.

`H` is the hash for the RFC 6979 nonce, normally the hash that made `digest`. A digest longer
than 521 bits is cut to its leftmost 521 bits, as ECDSA requires.

## `EcdsaP521Sha512`

```silk
pub struct EcdsaP521Sha512
```

Functions that verify ECDSA signatures on P-521 with SHA-512.

### When to use
Use it to verify a P-521 signature, for example in a certificate chain or a JSON Web Token with
`ES521`. To sign, use [`P521.sign`](#P521.impl.sign) and [`EcdsaP521.toDer`](#EcdsaP521.impl.toDer).

### Details
Public keys are 133 bytes in uncompressed SEC1 form: `0x04`, then the X and Y coordinates, each
66 bytes big-endian. Signatures are in DER form. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas
A valid signature proves only that the holder of the private key signed the message. It does not
prove that you can trust the key. To check a certificate chain, use the `silk.tls.trust_*`
modules.

<a id="EcdsaP521Sha512.impl"></a>

### Associated function `validatePublicKey`


Checks that `publicKey` is a valid uncompressed P-521 public key.

It must be 133 bytes: `0x04`, then X and Y, each 66 bytes big-endian and less than the field
prime, and the point must be on the curve.

#### Errors
- `InvalidKey` if it is not valid.

<a id="EcdsaP521Sha512.impl.verify"></a>

### Associated function `verify`

```silk
pub fn verify(publicKey: &[u8], message: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> Result<
    (),
    P521SignatureError,
  >
```

Checks that `signature` is a valid signature of `message` by `publicKey`.

`publicKey` is 133 bytes, uncompressed. `signature` is DER. The function hashes `message` with
SHA-512, so give the message, not its digest. Both high and low `s` values are accepted.

#### Errors
- `InvalidKey` or `InvalidEncoding` for input that is not valid.
- `AuthenticationFailed` if the signature does not match.

<a id="EcdsaP521Sha512.impl.verifyCertificate"></a>

### Associated function `verifyCertificate`

```silk
pub fn verifyCertificate<'key, 'sig>(
    keyAlgorithm: &AlgorithmView<'key>,
    publicKey: &BitStringView<'key>,
    message: &[u8],
    signatureAlgorithm: &AlgorithmView<'sig>,
    signature: &BitStringView<'sig>,
  ) -> Result<(), P521SignatureError>
```

Verifies a certificate signature from the parts that `silk.tls.certificate` reads.

`message` is the signed part of the certificate (the TBSCertificate DER). The key algorithm
must be `id-ecPublicKey` with the curve `secp521r1`, and the signature algorithm must be
`ecdsa-with-SHA512` with no parameters.

#### Errors
- `UnsupportedAlgorithm` or `InvalidParameters` if the algorithms do not match.
- `InvalidKey` or `InvalidEncoding` if the key or the signature is not valid.
- `AuthenticationFailed` if the signature does not match.

#### Gotchas
It checks only this one signature. It does not check the chain, the dates, or the names.

<a id="EcdsaP521"></a>

## `EcdsaP521`

```silk
pub struct EcdsaP521
```

ECDSA on P-521 with any hash, and conversion between the two signature forms.

### When to use
Use it to verify a signature made with a hash other than SHA-256, or a signature in the fixed
132-byte form (`r`, then `s`), as in JSON Web Tokens and WebCrypto. To sign, use [`P521.sign`](#P521.impl.sign).
For SHA-512 with DER signatures, as in TLS and X.509, [`EcdsaP521Sha512`](#EcdsaP521Sha512) is shorter.

### Details
Public keys are 133 bytes in uncompressed SEC1 form. A fixed-form signature is 132 bytes. A DER
signature is a SEQUENCE of the two INTEGERs, at most 139 bytes. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas
A valid signature proves only that the holder of the private key signed the message. It does not
prove that you can trust the key.

<a id="EcdsaP521.impl.verify"></a>

### Associated function `verify`

```silk
pub fn verify<H: Digest>(publicKey: &[u8], message: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> Result<
    (),
    P521SignatureError,
  >
```

Checks that `signature`, in the fixed 132-byte form, is a valid signature of `message`,
hashed with `H`, by `publicKey`.

Both high and low `s` values are accepted.

#### Errors
- `InvalidKey` if `publicKey` is not a valid uncompressed key.
- `InvalidEncoding` if `signature` is not 132 bytes, or `r` or `s` is not between 1 and the
  order of the curve.
- `AuthenticationFailed` if the signature does not match.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if `message` is longer than `H` allows.

<a id="EcdsaP521.impl.verifyDigest"></a>

```silk

    (),
    P521SignatureError,
  >
```

Checks that `signature`, in the fixed 132-byte form, is a valid signature by `publicKey` of a
message whose digest is `digest`.

A digest longer than 521 bits is cut to its leftmost 521 bits, as ECDSA requires.

#### Errors
- `InvalidKey`, `InvalidEncoding`, or `AuthenticationFailed`, as for [`EcdsaP521.verify`](#EcdsaP521.impl.verify).

#### Errors

  order of the curve.

<a id="EcdsaP521.impl.toDer"></a>

### Associated function `toDer`

```silk
pub fn toDer(signature: &[u8], output: &mut [u8]) -> usize
```

Writes the DER form of the fixed 132-byte signature `signature` to the start of `output`, and
returns its length, at most 139 bytes.

It does not check the values of `r` and `s`. The bytes of `output` after the DER do not
change.

#### Gotchas
The program traps if `signature` is not 132 bytes, or `output` is shorter than the DER.
